definition: Exacerbate means to make an existing problem worse or more intense.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word exacerbate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know exacerbate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Scratching only exacerbates the rash, carrying the itch from wrist to elbow by nightfall.
Hamper is the mildest setback — a hampered effort is slowed and inconvenienced but still on course, well short of the sharpened trouble exacerbate names.
Cripple goes further than exacerbate — an exacerbated supply line limps along in worse shape than before; a crippled one stops moving at all.

Worsen is the plain, everyday verb: anything at all can worsen, on its own or with help, whether or not trouble existed before. Exacerbate is choosier — it insists a problem was already there and names the push that made it sharper. Weather worsens; a curfew exacerbates a shortage.

To stoke is to feed something so it flares — a fire, a fear, a rumor — and it works even on small embers. To exacerbate is to sharpen a problem already burning in the open. Stoking feeds a thing fuel; exacerbating makes existing trouble crueler.

The trainer's log spent five words on it: injury present, play made it worse.
Exacerbate is the exact word for what the minutes on court did, because it means to make an existing problem worse or more intense — and existing is the load-bearing idea.
You cannot exacerbate a hamstring that was sound; the word requires trouble present first, then names the push that sharpens it.
Worsen is the loose everyday verb; trigger starts something new; exacerbate pours vinegar into a cut already open.
Exacerbate needs a problem already on the table — you exacerbate a shortage, a strain, a feud, never a blank slate.
Trigger and cause start things; worsen is the plain verb when register does not matter.
In this unit's terms: a blight destroys on its own, and careless handling exacerbates what the blight began.

When inspectors closed the Harbor Street bridge for emergency repairs, downtown traffic was already crawling through a summer of road work.
City planners knew the closure would exacerbate the congestion, but their models underestimated by half.
Drivers rerouted through neighborhoods never built for the volume, and delivery trucks idled three-deep outside the market.
